item.research_question: How does the addition of AlTiVZrCrMo high entropy alloy (HEA) as a reinforcement affect the mechanical properties and wear performance of LM13 aluminum alloy?
item.material_system: AlTiVZrCrMo high entropy alloy (HEA) reinforced LM13 aluminum alloy
item.processing_route: Stir casting with 10 wt. % of ball-milled equiatomic AlTiVZrCrMo HEA particles
item.test_conditions: Room temperature, applied load: 10-50 N, sliding distance: 500-2500 m, sliding velocity: 0.5-2.5 m/s
key_findings: Microhardness increased by 37.6% compared to LM13 alloy
Compressive strength increased by 73.3% compared to LM13 alloy
Tensile strength increased by 47.8% compared to LM13 alloy
Wear rate decreased with increasing sliding velocity beyond 1.5 m/s
Applied load is the most significant parameter affecting wear rate, followed by sliding distance and sliding velocity
item.mechanism: The addition of HEA particles refines the grain structure, increases dislocation density, and enhances solid solution strengthening, leading to improved mechanical properties and wear resistance
item.limitations: High cost of producing ball-milled HEA with uniform particle size, limited to dry sliding wear conditions
item.future_work: Optimizing the composite for real-world applications, exploring behavior under lubricated and high-temperature environments
quotes: The microhardness, compressive strength, and tensile strength of the Al/HEA composite are increased by 37.6, 73.3, and 47.8% over the LM 13 alloy
The applied load is the most significant parameter, followed by sliding distance and sliding velocity

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does the addition of AlTiVZrCrMo high entropy alloy (HEA) as a reinforcement affect the mechanical properties and wear performance of LM13 aluminum alloy?. System: AlTiVZrCrMo high entropy alloy (HEA) reinforced LM13 aluminum alloy. Processing: Stir casting with 10 wt. % of ball-milled equiatomic AlTiVZrCrMo HEA particles. Test conditions: Room temperature, applied load: 10-50 N, sliding distance: 500-2500 m, sliding velocity: 0.5-2.5 m/s. Findings: Microhardness increased by 37.6% compared to LM13 alloy; Compressive strength increased by 73.3% compared to LM13 alloy; Tensile strength increased by 47.8% compared to LM13 alloy; Wear rate decreased with increasing sliding velocity beyond 1.5 m/s; Applied load is the most significant parameter affecting wear rate, followed by sliding distance and sliding velocity. Mechanism: The addition of HEA particles refines the grain structure, increases dislocation density, and enhances solid solution strengthening, leading to improved mechanical properties and wear resistance. Limitations: High cost of producing ball-milled HEA with uniform particle size, limited to dry sliding wear conditions. Future work: Optimizing the composite for real-world applications, exploring behavior under lubricated and high-temperature environments. Quote: "The microhardness, compressive strength, and tensile strength of the Al/HEA composite are increased by 37.6, 73.3, and 47.8% over the LM 13 alloy"
